title: OpenAI Unveils Private Safety Processing for Zero Data Retention AI Deployments
content_md: OpenAI has previewed Private Safety Processing (PSP), a safety-monitoring architecture designed to identify misuse patterns across related AI interactions while preserving its Zero Data Retention (ZDR) commitment for eligible API customers. The approach addresses a growing enterprise dilemma: stronger frontier-model safeguards often require broader behavioral context, but retaining sensitive prompts and outputs can conflict with privacy, security, and regulatory obligations. Under OpenAI’s ZDR model, prompts and model responses are not retained after processing, customer content is unavailable for review by OpenAI personnel, and enterprise data is not used for model training unless the customer explicitly opts in. OpenAI Unveils Private Safety Processing The company says PSP is intended to extend safety analysis beyond the single-request scope of existing ZDR-compatible controls without exposing underlying customer content to human reviewers. Traditional safety systems can assess a single prompt or response for prohibited or harmful content. However, OpenAI argues that serious misuse may emerge only when activity is correlated across multiple interactions. Threat actors, for example, may distribute malicious intent across a sequence of seemingly benign prompts, repeatedly probe model safeguards, coordinate activity across accounts, or disguise harmful objectives as routine research.
